items.title: Closed runtime artifact envelope
items.statement: A valid instance is an object, rejects undeclared top-level properties, and must contain the twelve named envelope fields.

items.title: Artifact kind and schema identity are fixed
items.statement: The schema structurally identifies only version-one code_diff runtime artifacts through constant schema_id and artifact_type values.

items.title: Required identity inputs are nonempty strings
items.statement: artifact_id, project_id, run_id, and attempt_id are required and structurally constrained only to nonempty strings.

items.title: Authority and ownership are optional and unconstrained
items.statement: producer_ref and actor_ref are optional arbitrary strings; the contract does not require an accountable producer or actor, distinguish their authorities, or define ownership of creation and mutation.
items.impact: Artifacts may validate without attributable production authority or an enforceable ownership boundary.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent whether these references are required, how they resolve, and which authority checks apply.

items.title: No lifecycle states or transitions
items.statement: The declared required property set has no status, lifecycle state, supersession, invalidation, or transition fields and cannot express permitted artifact state transitions or preconditions.
items.impact: Consumers cannot determine from the contract whether a diff is pending, complete, failed, stale, revoked, or superseded.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent the lifecycle outside this artifact contract.

items.title: code_diff payload has no semantic contract
items.statement: type_payload may be any object with at least one property. The schema does not define patches, files, before or after identities, base or head revisions, hashes, binary changes, ordering, or apply semantics.
items.impact: Mutually incompatible payload shapes all validate, so consumers cannot reliably parse, display, verify, or apply the advertised code diff.
items.builder_discretion: Builders have effectively unrestricted discretion over the defining code_diff representation and behavior.

items.title: Creation timestamp is not validated as a timestamp
items.statement: created_at_utc requires only a nonempty string; neither date-time syntax nor UTC-zone semantics are enforced.
items.impact: Invalid or non-UTC values validate, undermining ordering, freshness, retention, and audit calculations.
items.builder_discretion: Producers and consumers must independently choose a timestamp grammar and UTC interpretation.

items.title: Projection state semantics are unconstrained
items.statement: projection_freshness and projection_health are required arbitrary strings with no enumerated states, derivation rules, transition rules, or relationship to created_at_utc.
items.impact: Producers can emit contradictory or uninterpretable projection condition labels and consumers cannot implement deterministic decisions.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must define vocabularies, derivation, precedence, and transition behavior.

items.title: Reference integrity and safe resolution are unspecified
items.statement: Contextual and content reference fields are arbitrary strings. The schema specifies no grammar, namespace, integrity hash, authorization scope, trust boundary, resolution failure behavior, or protection against unsafe locations.
items.impact: Consumers cannot safely or deterministically resolve referenced content or prove that it is the content the producer intended.
items.builder_discretion: Implementers must choose schemes, resolvers, access controls, integrity checks, and error handling.

items.title: Routing exists without propagation or consumer semantics
items.statement: routing_refs must contain at least one nonempty string, but duplicates are allowed and the contract names no consumers, routing authority, delivery guarantees, ordering, acknowledgement, retry, or fan-out behavior.
items.impact: Valid artifacts do not provide enough information for interoperable propagation or consumer handling.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent routing targets, delivery semantics, deduplication, acknowledgement, and retry policy.

items.title: Failure and recovery behavior is absent
items.statement: The closed artifact property contract provides no error, validation-failure, partial-diff, retry, recovery, revocation, or replacement representation.
items.impact: Failures cannot be represented or recovered consistently within the artifact model.
items.builder_discretion: Implementers must invent out-of-band failure and recovery protocols.

items.title: No scale or resource bounds
items.statement: Arrays and strings have no maximum sizes; type_payload has no maximum properties or nested complexity constraints; the contract sets no maximum diff size, file count, content size, or processing expectation.
items.impact: A schema-valid artifact may impose unbounded storage, transport, validation, rendering, or application cost.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose limits, streaming behavior, truncation, pagination, and rejection policy.

items.title: Version identity lacks compatibility and migration rules
items.statement: The schema declares a v1 identifier but specifies no forward or backward compatibility policy, unknown-version behavior, migration path, or schema negotiation mechanism.
items.impact: Version evolution may fragment producers and consumers despite a stable-looking identifier.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent version negotiation, migration, and rejection behavior.

items.title: Identity coherence across related fields is not enforced
items.statement: thread_id, node_id, provider_attempt_ref, usage_event_ref, receipt_refs, run_id, and attempt_id have only independent primitive constraints; no cross-field consistency or referential-existence oracle is defined.
items.impact: An artifact may validate while referring to unrelated, missing, or contradictory execution entities.
items.builder_discretion: Consumers must decide whether and how to verify referential consistency.

items.title: Retention and privacy policy are opaque
items.statement: retention_class is a required arbitrary string, while the schema provides no allowed classes, deletion schedule, legal-hold behavior, sensitivity classification, redaction rule, or authorization policy for code content and summaries.
items.impact: Sensitive source changes may be retained, exposed, or deleted inconsistently while still satisfying the schema.
items.builder_discretion: Operators must invent retention vocabularies, lifecycle actions, authorization, redaction, and audit behavior.

items.title: Structural JSON Schema validation is the explicit oracle
items.statement: The document declares JSON Schema draft 2020-12 and supplies structural constraints; conformance is machine-checkable but does not establish semantic correctness or applicability of the diff.

items.title: GUI truth is not represented by this contract
items.statement: The source is explicitly a Runtime Artifact code_diff object schema and contains no GUI presentation fields or user-interaction contract; GUI truth is not applicable within this isolated schema window.

items.title: Content location and payload precedence are ambiguous
items.statement: content_ref and detail_ref are optional while type_payload is required and unconstrained; the schema does not define whether references duplicate, supplement, or override inline payload data, nor what a consumer outputs when they disagree.
items.impact: Consumers can derive different code diffs from the same schema-valid artifact.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose authoritative content sources and conflict handling.

dimension_assessments.summary: Envelope validation behavior is explicit, but code-diff semantics and lifecycle behavior are not.
The schema identifies and structurally validates a code_diff artifact, but does not define a consumable diff capability.
Required envelope inputs are identified, but diff input/output representation, content precedence, and resulting consumer output are under-specified.
The top-level closed-object contract is exact; payload, references, timestamps, and cross-field invariants are not semantically contracted.
Projection labels exist without vocabularies, and no artifact lifecycle or transitions are represented.
Actor and producer references are optional unconstrained strings with no authority checks.
No accountable owner or mutation ownership boundary is defined.
Routing references exist, but consumers and their parsing, delivery, and acknowledgement obligations are absent.
This isolated source is an artifact object schema and specifies no GUI surface or interaction.
No failure state, diagnostic, retry, revocation, replacement, or recovery contract is present.
Reference resolution, authorization, integrity, sensitivity, redaction, and privacy handling are unspecified.
routing_refs is structurally required but propagation semantics are absent.
Projection and retention labels lack operational vocabularies, derivation, lifecycle action, and enforcement semantics.
No resource bounds or processing expectations constrain references, text, arrays, or payload complexity.
A v1 identifier is present without compatibility, negotiation, or migration rules.
Structural validation is explicit, but semantic diff correctness, applicability, reference integrity, and identity coherence oracles are absent.
Builders must invent the defining payload, lifecycle, authorities, routing, reference resolution, recovery, limits, compatibility, and content precedence.
Principal unknowns are payload meaning, reference semantics, state vocabularies, cross-field identity, and precedence between inline and referenced content.
